knowledge_chunks.title: Machine learning method notes
knowledge_chunks.text: Late delivery classification compares a simple baseline with a learned model on a later temporal holdout. Accuracy can be misleading when late orders are uncommon. Read precision, recall, F1, ROC AUC, class balance, and the confusion matrix together when available. A model has no demonstrated advantage until its measured holdout result is compared with the baseline.

knowledge_chunks.title: Machine learning method notes
knowledge_chunks.text: Delivery-duration regression predicts a continuous number of days. Mean absolute error (MAE) is expressed in days and describes the average absolute prediction error. Root mean squared error (RMSE) gives larger errors greater weight. R squared compares squared error with a constant-mean reference; it can be negative. Report only metrics actually computed by this run.

knowledge_chunks.title: Machine learning method notes
knowledge_chunks.text: Temporal evaluation trains on earlier orders and holds out later orders. Fit preprocessing inside the training pipeline. Post-outcome reviews and delivered timestamps leak future information into order-time predictions. Hyperparameter choices require a validation set or inner time-aware cross-validation; a final holdout should stay untouched until evaluation.

knowledge_chunks.title: Machine learning method notes
knowledge_chunks.text: The default document retriever uses local TF-IDF lexical similarity and returns source-linked excerpts. It does not use semantic embeddings or a generative language model. Search quality should be evaluated with independently authored question/relevant-source pairs; citation presence alone does not prove an answer is supported.

knowledge_chunks.title: Machine learning method notes
knowledge_chunks.text: Model feature rankings describe predictive associations in the evaluated dataset. They cannot establish causal business drivers. Synthetic records can validate software behavior but cannot prove real commercial performance. Forecasting, recommendation models, streaming, and fine-tuning are future extensions unless their implementations and evaluations are present.

knowledge_chunks.title: Olist historical demonstration workspace
knowledge_chunks.text:
The workspace uses the historical Brazilian E-Commerce Public Dataset published by Olist: https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/olistbr/brazilian-ecommerce . The publisher's release announcement is https://www.kaggle.com/general/67613 . Preserve its CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 attribution and terms; the DataPilot code license does not replace the dataset license.

This is an offline demonstration using historical marketplace records. It is not a connection to a current Olist service or an endorsement by Olist. Source dates retain the source clock representation; no timezone was established from these files.

knowledge_chunks.title: Olist historical demonstration workspace
knowledge_chunks.text: Classification predicts whether an eligible delivered order arrived after its estimated calendar delivery date. Regression predicts observed days from purchase to delivery. Filtering to delivered orders excludes canceled and undelivered orders, so these results do not establish performance on every newly placed order. Inputs must be available at the stated prediction time. Review text, actual delivery time and rating are outcomes and must not be order-time prediction inputs.

knowledge_chunks.title: Olist historical demonstration workspace
knowledge_chunks.text:
Review text is Portuguese. The text classifier predicts a rating group from the comment: ratings 1–2 are called negative, 3 neutral, and 4–5 positive. These names are proxies defined by the recorded ratings; they are not independently annotated sentiment labels. A chronological holdout uses review answer timestamps. Vocabulary and IDF are fitted on training text only.

The review analysis keeps the earliest answered review per order, then excludes missing comments or invalid ratings. This means comment authors need not represent all customers. Complaint counts use overlapping keyword rules among low-rating comments. They describe matched phrases rather than measured root causes or validated topic classifications.

knowledge_chunks.title: Olist historical demonstration workspace
knowledge_chunks.text:
The public evidence library contains only a bounded selection of repeated short review phrases with contact/address patterns excluded. It is a demonstration retrieval corpus, not a representative or complete review archive. Answers should identify original Portuguese excerpts and their source; DataPilot does not claim to have independently verified customer statements.

Any separate example operations policy in this repository is authored fictional demonstration material. It is not an actual Olist refund, shipping, or customer-service policy. Do not merge those fictional policy statements into claims about Olist.

filtering.deduplication: Earliest answered review per order, before excluding missing comment text.

review_analysis.selection_method: Predeclared text baseline; no holdout-driven tuning.
review_analysis.confusion_matrix_axes: Rows are actual labels, columns predicted labels, in labels order.
limitations: Targets are rating groups (1–2 negative, 3 neutral, 4–5 positive), not independently annotated sentiment.
Identical wording can carry different ratings, so a positive-sounding phrase may appear in a low-rating group.
Review text is Portuguese source material. No translation or universal multilingual accuracy is claimed.
Only earliest answered reviews with nonempty comments enter evaluation; text reviewers may differ from all customers.
Common wording may repeat across train and holdout. The model has not been evaluated on a different marketplace.
Complaint themes use overlapping keyword rules on low-rating comments; they are descriptive matches, not validated topic labels or causal findings.
Published excerpts are a bounded set of repeated short phrases selected from the heldout period and filtered for contact/address patterns; they are not a representative review sample.
These are historical offline results. Scikit-learn inference runs locally; the public site shows saved text-model metrics and retrieval evidence.
